decisive_items: Rhythmic epileptiform discharges originating from the right frontal area with ipsilateral hemispheric spreading and relatively limited homologous contralateral involvement.
episodes of prominent dizziness, vertigo, intermittent left arm shaking, and bouts of dull response
Activities appeared in a quasi-periodic fashion at intervals of about one second, during which the patient presented significant dizziness, vertigo and dull response.
response.rationale: EEG shows right frontal epileptiform discharges time-locked to the episodes, establishing a seizure origin; recurrent brief attacks with impaired awareness and left arm shaking are characteristic of frontal lobe epilepsy. Hypertension and MRI white matter changes are nonspecific, and absence of prior seizures does not exclude new-onset epilepsy.

rejected.why: No focal brainstem signs and MRI shows no posterior circulation/brainstem signal; EEG epileptiform discharges favor seizure over TIA.
Hypertensive BP and epileptiform EEG are inconsistent with vasovagal syncope.
No headache or migrainous features; EEG shows epileptiform discharges.
No true loss of consciousness and EEG demonstrates seizure activity.
Less specific than frontal lobe epilepsy; left arm shaking and right frontal discharges point to frontal lobe origin.
BP elevation is present but episodic symptoms are time-locked to epileptiform discharges, not hypertensive encephalopathy.
MRI lacks posterior circulation/brainstem signal changes and EEG shows epileptiform activity.
